parts.meaning: The air fryer runs hotter than the dial says, because the fan pushes hot air straight onto the food. Dropping 25F keeps the top from browning before the centre sets.
The fan cooks food about 20 percent faster than still oven air, so the air fryer time is four fifths of the oven time.
The check-at time is 70 percent of the oven time. Open the basket then and test with a toothpick.
If the top browns before the centre sets, tent the pan loosely with foil and let the centre finish.

formula.text: Air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F. Air fryer time = oven time × 0.8. Check at = oven time × 0.7. For baked goods at 350F for 25 minutes: 325F for 20 minutes, check at 18 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the oven settings
howToSteps.text: Find the temperature and time in your recipe. Most bakes go in at 350F, for 20 to 30 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Convert both numbers
howToSteps.text: Take 25F off the temperature and take 20 percent off the time. 350F for 25 minutes becomes 325F for 20 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Pick a pan that fits
howToSteps.text: Use a pan with space around it for the air to move, and fill it no more than two thirds full.

howToSteps.name: Bake and check early
howToSteps.text: Start checking at 18 minutes with a toothpick. Tent with foil if the top darkens before the centre sets.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Cakes and Bakes
tutorial: Small bakes are the quiet talent of the air fryer. Muffins, cookies, and a small banana bread bake well in a pan that fits the basket, and they bake faster than the oven does. A bake that goes in at 350F for 25 minutes air fries at 325F for 20 minutes. Start checking at 18 minutes.

The top is the thing to watch. The heating element sits just above the food, so the top of a cake browns much faster than the centre sets. If the top darkens early, tent the pan loosely with foil and let the centre finish. The foil goes on with the food holding it down, never loose in an empty basket, because the fan lifts loose foil into the element.

Bakes are also the food where the rule bends most. Some baking guides drop the temperature by 50F instead of 25F, because batter rises and sets differently in moving hot air. This converter uses the standard 25F drop, and the check-at time is the safety net. If your bakes keep browning too fast on top, drop another 25F next time and keep the converted time.

Use a pan that fits with air around it. The basket needs space for the hot air to move, so a pan that touches the sides bakes unevenly. A six-inch round pan fits most baskets, and silicone muffin cups fit where a metal tin does not. Fill the pan no more than two thirds full, because batter rises toward the element.

The toothpick test still decides. A cake is done when a toothpick in the centre comes out with a few moist crumbs, not wet batter. The converted time gets you close. The toothpick tells you when to stop.
